question: In the unsignalized midblock-crosswalk example in Figure 3B-16, how far in advance of the crosswalk are the yield lines shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B (unsignalized midblock crosswalk) of Figure 3B-16, the yield lines (with the accompanying Yield Here to Pedestrians R1-5 signs) are shown 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk. This matches the MUTCD Guidance that yield (stop) lines and their signs be placed 20 to 50 feet in advance of the nearest edge of the crosswalk on uncontrolled multi-lane approaches. Standards (mandatory): - "Yield Here to (Stop Here for) Pedestrians (R1-5, R1-5a, R1-5b, R1-5c, R1-5d, and R1-5e) signs (see Figure 2B-2) shall be used if yield (stop) lines are used in advance of a marked crosswalk only where it crosses an uncontrolled multi-lane approach." Guidance (recommended): - "If yield (stop) lines and Yield Here to (Stop Here for) Pedestrians signs are used in advance of a crosswalk that crosses an uncontrolled multi-lane approach, the signs should be placed 20 to 50 feet in advance of the nearest edge of the crosswalk (see Section 3B.19 and Figure 3B-16)." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3B-16, Drawing B ("Unsignalized midblock crosswalk"), shows a dimension callout of "20 to 50 ft" between the staggered yield lines/R1-5 sign location and the crosswalk; Drawing C ("Crosswalk across ramp") shows the same "20 to 50 ft" dimension. [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 3B-16 confirms the "20 to 50 ft" dimensions in both Drawings B and C. Citations: - Section 2B.19 Guidance §3 (p.81) - Section 2B.19 Standard §2 (p.81) - Figure 3B-16 (p.574)
gold_answer: 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk.
